mu_name: The wave a Power Wave throws
mu_name_from:
ZzzOpenData.cpp:4166: `AccessModel(MODEL_MAGIC2, L"Data\\Skill\\", L"Magic", 2)` - so Data/Skill/Magic02.bmd. Filed under Skill with the meteor, the bones and the arrows, because in MU everything a spell puts in the air is an effect model rather than a thing in the world.

Not Magic01.bmd, which is a different model in the same folder, and not MagicCircle01.bmd. The loader builds the name from a stem and a number and the number is what tells them apart.
mesh_from:
muextract export-obj on Data/Skill/Magic02.bmd, from MuMain. Sixteen triangles in a single mesh, twenty-four vertices, all of it on magic_g.jpg.

One mesh is the fact that matters, because the client's `o->BlendMesh = 0` names mesh zero as the blended one and there is no other: the whole model is additive, with nothing solid inside it. The meteor is the other shape of thing - a solid rock at mesh 0 with an additive cone at mesh 1 - and reading this one the same way would have you looking for a core that does not exist.

Measured off the export, in metres: 0.91 across, 2.44 tall, 3.18 deep. It is a curtain and not a ball, and it is long from front to back - it runs 2.01 m behind its own origin and 1.17 m ahead of it, so most of the model trails the point it is drawn at.

parts.note:
Data/Skill/magic_g.OZJ, 128 by 64 and fully opaque - the wide shape is the point rather than an accident, because the client scrolls this sheet along the model as it flies.

Additive because the client says which mesh: `o->BlendMesh = 0` is the first line of the MODEL_MAGIC2 arm of CreateEffect, and zero is this only mesh. Nothing here is drawn any other way.

It has no alpha channel, which is what an additive sheet in MU normally looks like on disk: black is transparent because black adds nothing, and the shape is carried entirely in the brightness.

blend_from: `o->BlendMesh = 0` in ZzzEffect.cpp:1991, outside any sub-type ladder, so it holds for every Power Wave in the game. The brightness is not constant: the mover sets `o->BlendMeshLight = o->LifeTime * 0.1f` every frame, which starts at 2.0 with a twenty-frame life - saturating, on MU's GL_ONE, GL_ONE blend - and falls to nothing as it goes. So the wave leaves at full and dims across its whole flight rather than at the end of it.
scale_from:
**Nine tenths, and it is not a choice anybody made for this spell.** The MODEL_MAGIC2 arm of CreateEffect sets no `o->Scale` at all - it sets a blend mesh, a lifetime and a direction and stops - so the model keeps whatever CreateEffect gives it. That is not one:

    float Scale = 0.0f          // the declared default, ZzzEffect.h:66
    ...
    if (Scale <= 0.0f) o->Scale = 0.9f;
    else               o->Scale = Scale;

The call is `CreateEffect(MODEL_MAGIC2, o->Position, Angle, o->Light)` with no scale argument, so it takes the zero, fails the test and lands on nine tenths. Read as 'no scale line means scale one' this comes out a tenth too big, which was the first thing wrong with it here.

The two spells built before this one hide the rule rather than showing it: the meteor and the fireball both roll `o->Scale` explicitly in their own arms, so neither ever reaches the default. Power Wave is the first effect in this project that does.
frames_from: `o->LifeTime = 20` in the same arm - four fifths of a second at MU's clock, and Energy Ball's lifetime exactly.
lift_from:
There is none, and the absence is deliberate rather than an omission in the reading.

The bolt gets `o->Position[2] += 100` and the fireball `+= 120`; this arm sets no position at all, so the effect is created at `o->Position` - the caster's feet, which in MU is the terrain height under him. The model agrees: its geometry runs from y = 0 to y = 2.44 m, authored standing on the ground rather than centred on an origin. A wave that leaves at chest height would be a wave floating over the field, and this one is a sheet sweeping across it.
flight_from:
`Vector(0.f, -60.f, 0.f, o->Direction)` in the same arm, turned by the angle the effect was created with, and integrated by the default `MoveParticle(o, true)` - MODEL_MAGIC2 has no arm of its own in the movement switch. Sixty units a reference frame is fifteen tiles a second, which is Energy Ball's speed exactly.

Flat. The direction has no vertical term, so a wave thrown at something on a hill sweeps past it at the height it left rather than climbing.
passes_through_from:
**It does not end on its target, and this is the one thing that makes it a different shape of effect from the other two.**

The fireball and the bolt both call CheckTargetRange from their movers, which pins the lifetime to one inside a hundred units of the body. Move_MODEL_MAGIC2 does not call it. It does not test the terrain either, and MODEL_MAGIC2 appears nowhere in EffectDestructor - so nothing whatever happens at the far end. The wave runs its twenty frames out, which at sixty a frame is 1200 units, and vanishes.

Twelve tiles, against a spell whose range is six. So it visibly carries on for as far again past whatever it was aimed at, and that is the picture: a wave sweeping through and away rather than a missile arriving.
sounds_from: One, and it is not this spell's own: `PlayBuffer(SOUND_MAGIC)` on the line after the effect is made. SOUND_MAGIC is Data/Sound/sMagic.wav, which Energy Ball already plays and which this project already carries as `spell_magic`. Played at the cast rather than at the arrival, which is where every skill's wave goes except the bolt's.
not_built_note: Sub-type 2 is not this. The MODEL_MAGIC2 creation arm has one branch - `if (o->SubType == 2) o->Weapon = CharacterMachine->PacketSerial++` - and the mover has a whole second half behind the same test: a hidden mesh, an eleventh smoke sub-type, two BITMAP_SHINY sprites and a BITMAP_LIGHT lifted fifty units. That is the owned, serial-numbered variant ZzzCharacter.cpp:2829 makes five of at once, and it belongs to whatever throws those rather than to Power Wave. The player's is sub-type 0 and takes none of it.
